extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, in-house counsel, and parties seeking a patent infringement damages expert witness
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and quantification of patent infringement damages (reasonable royalty and related measures) using the 15 Georgia‑Pacific factors and related evidentiary and expert‑qualification considerations. Intended to guide expert testimony and damages consulting in patent litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalties patentee receives for licensing the patent in suit
rubrics_metrics.description: Royalties patentee receives for licensing the patent in suit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider historic license payments received by the patentee for the patent-in-suit as direct evidence of a reasonable rate; supports the background level of compensation the patentee has accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rates the licensee pays for other comparable patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates the licensee pays for use of other comparable to the patent in suit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare licensing rates paid for comparable patents to support minimum royalty rates or per-unit royalties across scenarios (hardware, software, etc.). Use comparable-license analysis to justify a negotiated rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and scope of the license (exclusivity, territory, customer restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and scope of license in terms of exclusivity and territory / customer restrictions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether licenses were exclusive or non‑exclusive, geographic or field restrictions, and customer limits — these terms affect the value of a license and thus the reasonable royalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensor’s policy and marketing program to maintain patent monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensor’s established policy and marketing program to maintain patent monopoly by not licensing others to use the invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the patentee deliberately restricted licensing to preserve monopoly value; such a policy increases the economic value of the patent and influences royalty expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial relationship between licensor and licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial relationship between licensor and licensee, such as whether they are competitors or inventor and promoter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prior or existing business ties, competition, or promotional relationships between the parties; these relationships can affect bargaining positions and agreed royalty terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patented specialty on sales of other products (convoyed sales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of selling the patented specialty in promoting sales of other products of the licensee; the existing value of the invention to the licensor as a generator of sales of his non-patented items; and the extent of such derivative or convoyed sales
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether the patented feature drives incremental sales of other non‑patented products (convoyed or derivative sales) and quantify that effect when attributing value to the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of the patent and term of license
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of patent and term of license
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for remaining patent life and contemplated license term — longer remaining duration generally increases the present value of a royalty stream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established profitability, commercial success and popularity of products under the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Established profitability of the products made under the patent, its commercial success and its current popularity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use profitability metrics, sales data, market acceptance and popularity as indicia of the patent's value when allocating a portion of returns to the patented invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility and advantages of the patented property over old modes and devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility and advantages of patent property over old modes and devices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technical superiority, efficiency gains, cost savings, or other advantages the patented invention provides relative to prior art; these advantages inform the incremental value attributable to the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of the patented invention and its commercial embodiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of the patented invention; the character of the commercial embodiment of it as owned and produced by the licensor; and the benefit of those who have used the invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the invention is implemented commercially and document benefits realized by users to support claims about the invention's value and the appropriate royalty base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of the infringer’s use of the invention and value of such use
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the infringer has made use of the invention and the value of such use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify the infringer’s actual use (units, duration, scope) and the economic value derived from that use to determine the appropriate compensatory award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portion of profit or selling price customarily allowed for the use of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion of profit or selling price customarily allowed for the use of the invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on industry norms or customary splits to determine what fraction of profit or price is typically paid for comparable patented features; useful as a starting point in apportionment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portion of realizable profit attributable to the invention (apportionment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion of realizable profit attributable to the invention as distinguished from non-patented elements, significant features / improvements added by the infringer, the manufacturing process or business risks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform careful apportionment to isolate profits due to the patented feature versus other factors (non‑patented components, improvements, manufacturing efficiencies, market risk). Avoid over‑attribution to the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion testimony of qualified experts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualified expert analysis and testimony to explain valuation methodologies, apportionment, damages calculations, and the application of Georgia‑Pacific factors; expert credentials and methodology are critical for admissibility and persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome from a hypothetical arm’s-length negotiation (the Georgia‑Pacific 'book of wisdom')
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome from hypothetical arm’s length negotiation at the time of infringement began
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model the hypothetical negotiation between a willing licensor and willing licensee at the time infringement began to derive the reasonable royalty; consider bargaining positions, available alternatives, and the Georgia‑Pacific factors as inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages measures: adequate compensation, reasonable royalty, and lost profits
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘…adequate compensation for the infringement…’ ‘…reasonable royalty…’ ‘…lost profits…’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to evaluate and quantify different damages remedies under 35 U.S.C. §284 — including reasonable royalties and lost profits — selecting the appropriate measure(s) based on the facts and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and application of Georgia‑Pacific case law
rubrics_metrics.description: The most common framework for determining a reasonable royalty was set forth in Georgia‑Pacific Corp. v. United States Plywood Corp.; the court enumerated fifteen factors relevant to reasonable royalty awards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground analyses in the Georgia‑Pacific framework and subsequent Federal Circuit treatment (e.g., Unisplay v. American Electronic Sign Co.), using the fifteen factors as the standard checklist while applying modern apportionment and admissibility principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and domain expertise in relevant technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Expertise in horizontal technology and medical / healthcare specific patents and intellectual property, database software including indexing algorithms, software distribution and encryption algorithms, cDNA and related medical uses, healthcare software (EHRs, e-prescribing, clinical decision support), medication management, medical coding encoders, computer-assisted coding, and related areas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated subject matter expertise in the relevant technical field(s) is required to assess functionality, comparability, market impact, and to credibly apportion value in technology‑specific disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court qualification and acceptance as a damages expert
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Infringement Damages Expert Georgia Pacific Factors Certified by Federal Judge as Damages expert
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court recognition or prior rulings qualifying the expert to testify on damages (e.g., being declared qualified to testify in a federal circuit or district court) strengthens the expert’s role and admissibility in litigation.
